raw_response:
I am old now, and there are only two of us at home, so this year I will not spread myself too thin on the most labor-heavy work. I still plant several kinds, same as before, because one crop alone is not safe. Maize is my steady one, cotton can still bring cash if the year is decent, and mungbean and peanut give me some flexibility. I do not read books, I farm by what I have seen on my own land. If I put too little fertilizer, the crop looks weak and I regret saving that money. But if I spend too much at the start, then later I have no cash for water, pesticide, or family needs. So I will do it the old way: not too little, not too much, mostly like last year, with a bit more care on maize and a bit less money sunk into the smaller crops.

For water, I have the well, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate just because I can. I will water when the crop is at an important stage and the soil is dry. Cotton takes a lot of hand work, especially picking, so I will keep that area moderate. Maize is easier for me to manage, so I give it the biggest piece. Mungbean and peanut do not need as much fertilizer, and if one crop has a bad year, maybe the others help me out. That is how I keep the year steady.
